newsitem.title: TRINIDAD AND TOBAGO: Hindus in Trinidad worry over calypso in schools.
newsitem.headline: Hindus in Trinidad worry over calypso in schools.

text.p: Trinidadian Hindus were up in arms on Thursday over a movement to make the study of calypso music a compulsory subject in the Caribbean nation's primary schools.

"We strongly object to any compulsion on this matter, which must be a matter of choice for parents and school boards," Sat Maharaj, secretary-general of the Sanatan Dharma Maha Sabha, one of Trinidad's largest Hindu organisations, said in a statement.
Trinidad dates its unique musical form, calypso, back to the 18th century, and the bright, uptempo music is an important part of the annual winter Carnival festival.

The Caribbean News Agency reported that Trinidad Minister of Culture Daphne Phillips said last weekend that in recognition of calypso's contribution to life in Trinidad her office had a proposal to "inculcate the calypso art form at the level of the primary school."

The Hindu group said teaching calypso in schools would be a "unilateral totalitarian cultural imposition" and Trinidad would do better to focus on preventing illiteracy, innumeracy and juvenile crime.
Trinidad's population is about 40 percent black and 40 percent Indian, most of them Hindus. The remainder of the population of about 1.3 million is of mixed race, white, Syrian and Chinese.
